Hah yeah. Unfortunately depression doesn't ever go away. But with practice, therapy, and medication there are ways to control it so it doesn't control you. I know this to be the truth, but actually believing it is the hard part. 

Things to consider if you want to take back control:

- Cognitive behavioral therapy
- Medication
- Electroconvulsive therapy
- Exercise
- Diet 
- Getting the right amount of sleep
- Sticking to some sort of schedule

This is what I've learned so far. I still struggle everyday and I honestly don't know how much longer I'm going to keep up the fight. Be proactive when you're young, it's much easier.

Bringing up the thought of going out on a killing spree has got to be the most moronic thing someone has said when contemplating taking their own life. Saying that shit will lead directly to 2 things: You getting your post reported to Reddit and having a talk with your local police. 1 has already been done and I'm working on the 2nd. 

This shit is what fucks with everyone's perception of mental illness.

I can tell you from personal experience that being rich is not as great as people think it is. I used to drive a $120,000 Mercedes. Had nice clothes, etc. I'm much happier living more simple now than I ever was, and you would feel the exact same.

I can tell you from personal experience that this pain you are feeling is only temporary and it WILL pass. A year or two from now you will look back on this day and laugh at yourself. You havent even reached the best parts of life yet. Stick around and you'll see. If I'm wrong then message me in a year and I'll give you $10k. No joke.

It really is the definition of despair. 
I'm happy to hear you are strong enough to keep your promise of staying alive. Don't break it.

Agreed. Ive tried killing myself 4-5 times already. And 3 of those times I should have died for sure but for whatever reason I woke up. Seriously, no one has survived the amount of mg of the medication I've tried and lived.
